v1_problem: Since August 2026, billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled (590→1180→1260/month, E-07) primarily because the billing import/validation step of the meter-to-cash process is producing incorrect bills on accounts with ACTUAL meter reads (1,785 of 3,025 disputed bills) more often than on estimate-substituted bills (1,240) (E-01). This rules out slower ticket handling as the driver (response times stay within the 3.0-day SLA, E-02) and points away from read-collection failure as the dominant cause, leaving a defect in bill production from valid reads as the best-supported mechanism; a reported field-staffing shortfall (E-04/E-06) separately explains part of the smaller estimated-read-bill cohort.
v2_problem: Since billing import rule BV-17 (a high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none') was deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled (590→1180→1260/month, E-07); for the disputed ESTIMATED-read-cohort bills, 95.5% (1,184/1,240) had an AMI read received and exported before cutoff but were rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12), consistent with BV-17 misreading v4.2-firmware meters' '0.1 m3'-unit register values (versus legacy v3.x whole-m3 units, E-14) as abnormally high, triggering estimate substitution for valid consumption.
